Curriculum › Year 4

Year 4: what your child practises

In Year 4, Sharpwise has 35 topics in maths and 17 topics in English. Each one is below in plain words, with ideas to try at home.

Year 4 topics follow the National Curriculum for England. This page is made from the game's own list of topics, so it changes when the game does.

Play Sharpwise

Maths in Year 4

35 topics, grouped by the part of the curriculum each one practises.

Number: number and place value

Count in 6s, 7s, 9s, 25s and 1,000s
Count in 6s, 7s, 9s, 25s, 1,000s; 1,000 more or less
Negative Numbers
Count backwards through 0 to negative numbers
Place Value, Compare & Order
Place value of 4-digit numbers; compare and order beyond 1,000
Rounding & Estimating
Round to the nearest 10, 100 or 1,000; estimate on a number line
Roman Numerals to 100
Roman numerals to 100 (I to C); zero and place value

Try at home:

  • Count stairs, spoons or steps together, then count backwards, and stop to ask what comes next.
  • Make numbers from pairs of playing cards and ask which digit stands for tens and which for ones.

Number: addition and subtraction

Column Add & Subtract
Column addition and subtraction to 4 digits; inverse to check
Spot the mistake
Find the column with the mistake in a worked addition or subtraction
Two-Step Problems
Two-step problems in contexts, deciding which operations to use
Which operation?
Decide which operation solves a one-step problem, and why

Try at home:

  • Add the prices of two snacks in your head, then take one away to check the answer.

Number: multiplication and division

Times Tables to 12 × 12
Multiplication and division facts to 12 × 12
6× table
6 times table
7× table
7 times table
9× table
9 times table
11× table
11 times table
12× table
12 times table
Mental Multiplying
× 0, × 1, ÷ 1, derived facts, three numbers
Factor Pairs
Factor pairs and commutativity in mental calculations
Short Multiplication
2- and 3-digit × 1-digit, formal written method
Multiply & Scale Problems
Distributive law, scaling and correspondence problems

Try at home:

  • Set out egg boxes or muffin trays and count the rows and columns to find the lots of.
  • Add the prices of two snacks in your head, then take one away to check the answer.
  • Arrange 12 buttons into equal rows in different ways and see which sizes fit.

Number: fractions (including decimals)

Equivalent Fractions
Families of equivalent fractions, using diagrams
Hundredths
Count in hundredths; tenths ÷ 10
Fractions of Amounts
Fractions of quantities, including non-unit fractions
Add & Subtract Fractions
Add and subtract, same denominator, beyond one whole
Decimals & Fractions
Decimal equivalents of tenths, hundredths, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4
Divide by 10 & 100
÷ 10 and ÷ 100; ones, tenths and hundredths
Compare & Round Decimals
Round 1-dp decimals; compare and order to 2 dp
Pounds & Pence
Money in decimals to 2 dp; money problems

Try at home:

  • Cut a pizza or an apple into equal parts and ask for one half, one quarter or three quarters.
  • Read prices and measurements aloud: say what the digit after the point means, in tenths or hundredths.
  • Make numbers from pairs of playing cards and ask which digit stands for tens and which for ones.
  • Put two heaps of socks or coins side by side and ask which has more, and by how many.
  • Let your child pay with real coins at the shop and work out the change together.

Measurement

Converting Units
Convert between units
Area and Perimeter
Area by counting squares, perimeter
12- and 24-hour Time
Analogue, 12- and 24-hour clocks

Try at home:

  • Compare a cup, a jug and a bowl: which holds more? Use a ruler or shoe-lengths to measure the table.
  • Ask what the clock will say in half an hour, then check when the time comes.

Geometry: properties of shapes

Triangles and Quadrilaterals
Classify triangles and quadrilaterals
Acute and Obtuse Angles
Acute, obtuse, compare and order angles
Lines of Symmetry
Lines of symmetry, complete a symmetric figure

Try at home:

  • Go on a shape hunt around the house for circles, boxes, cylinders and right angles.

Geometry: position and direction

Coordinates
Describe positions as coordinates in the first quadrant, translate a point, complete a polygon

Try at home:

  • Go on a shape hunt around the house for circles, boxes, cylinders and right angles.

Statistics

Bar Charts & Time Graphs
Read bar charts, time graphs and tables; comparison, sum and difference problems

Try at home:

  • Tally the cars passing the window or the colours of socks, then say which has most and fewest.

English in Year 4

17 topics, grouped by the part of the curriculum each one practises.

Reading: comprehension

Retrieving Information
Retrieve and record information from non-fiction
Words in Context
Explaining the meaning of words in context

Try at home:

  • After a bedtime story, ask who it was about, what happened and where, then how many or why.
  • Add the prices of two snacks in your head, then take one away to check the answer.

Writing: vocabulary, grammar and punctuation

Plural and Possessive -s
